description: Henri II pledges Anzeling (high, middle and low justice) to Henriette de Vaudémont, January 1624.
Hestroff pledged to Henriette de Vaudémont; p. 51 says January 1624, p. 50 January 1625.
February 1620: the Conseil d'État maintains the abbot of Freistroff in the middle and low justice against the ducal procurator's claim of 1616.
Accommodation of 28-30 July 1620 between Lorraine and Trier confirms undivided joint sovereignty and common justice; approved by Ferdinand II on 4 December 1623.
Same accommodation of July 1620 for the Merzig part of the condominium.
Judgment of the Imperial Chamber of Speyer, 7 July 1629: the castle and town of Sarrewerden, as masculine fiefs of Metz, go to François II.
Same Speyer judgment of 7 July 1629 for Bouquenom.
31 July 1629: Lorraine troops take Bouquenom by force and occupy the whole county, beyond what the judgment granted.
François II dies 14 October 1632; Charles IV takes the oath of the county's subjects the next day.
